description: Israel Railways will run three trains per hour to and from Jerusalem during rush hours, up from two, starting Nov. 29, the company announced on Thursday. It is the first such upgrade since the high-speed line opened in 2018, according to the railway. The expanded service will operate from 6 a.m. to 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. to 7 p.m., connecting the capital with Ben-Gurion International Airport, Tel Aviv, Herzliya and Netanya. Netanya station will get five trains per hour at peak times, while two more morning trains will run between Jerusalem and Modi'in. Israel Railways said the expansion was made possible by a new signaling system designed to improve train frequency, punctuality and safety.

Kroizer pointed out that MKs from both parties walked out of the plenum during the singing of "Hatikvah," Israel's national anthem, as part of the Knesset's swearing-in ceremony last week. "It is a slap in the face to the fallen soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces, the victims of terror, and those currently serving in the IDF," he said, adding that lawmakers who "glorify 'martyrs'" and refuse to condemn the Hamas terror group are now "playing a decisive role" in the Knesset. Kroizer called Kahana, a former Israeli Air Force pilot who served as religious services minister under then-Prime Minister Naftali Bennett in 2021 and 2022, "a worthy individual who has contributed greatly to the state." However, the speaker was elected with the votes of "Tibi, Abbas, and their associates," Kroizer said. He noted the Arab lawmakers had dedicated their gains in the Oct. 27 election to "their 'brothers,' the Nukhba terrorists in Gaza." "This badge of shame will remain with him forever," Kroizer said. "It must be clear to the public that these parties do not seek the well-being of Israel's citizens; rather, time and again, they align themselves with those who seek our destruction," he added. "We will challenge this using parliamentary and public tools, fight against these decisions, and remind the public of the gap between pre-election promises and actions taken in the Knesset."

title: Knesset votes to extend longstanding state of emergency
description: Knesset lawmakers voted 8-1 on Wednesday to extend Israel's national state of emergency until March 18, 2027, the parliament said. The plenum approved a recommendation by the temporary Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, following a government request. The declaration is usually renewed for a year, but the temporary committee formed after the Oct. 27 Knesset election can only approve four-month extensions, Hebrew media reported. The declaration has been in effect since the Jewish state's founding in 1948, when the Provisional State Council issued it. It lets the government enact emergency regulations that can override Knesset legislation, subject to legal limits. It also keeps certain laws and orders that depend on the emergency in force.

From Gaza ceasefire negotiations to U.S.-Israel relations and from Iran’s nuclear ambitions to the war on terror, Blum and Regev dissect the week’s headlines with authority, candor and a touch of humor. title: A century of hope: How global medical breakthroughs shape the future of healthcare
description: Imagine being told you will never walk again, and then, through sheer resilience and world-class care, taking your very first steps. Imagine waiting for a lifesaving medical treatment that does not yet exist, only to benefit from a pioneering discovery that completely rewrites your future. Every day at Hadassah hospitals in Jerusalem, these inspiring stories unfold. Behind every outcome is a dedicated team of physicians, researchers and innovators pushing the boundaries of medicine. From complex, groundbreaking surgeries to vital advances in treatments for diseases affecting people across the globe, the impact extends far beyond borders. Hadassah, The Women’s Zionist Organization of America , powers the work of the hospitals through the collective strength of 300,000 members, Associates and supporters. It is a life-changing force for those who heal and for those who help make that healing possible. An international impact driven by research and care The scale of care delivered at Hadassah hospitals is immense. Each year, the organization serves more than 1 million patients, touching the lives of 1 in 10 Israelis. In 2025 alone, Hadassah hospitals welcomed 19,007 newborns into the world; performed 51,882 surgeries with precision care; launched nearly 2,000 clinical trials; and were awarded 25 new patents. The cutting-edge care is transformational. Take the story of Jonathan, a father of three who suffered severe, life-threatening trauma following a major highway accident. Transferred directly to the Level 1 trauma center at Hadassah Hospital Ein Kerem, his survival depended on an intricate, multistage surgical intervention led by an interdisciplinary team. Today, he is back home with his family, which is a testament to the hospital’s world-renowned emergency response and medical ingenuity. Whether pioneering research in cancer, ALS, Alzheimer’s disease or trauma medicine, Hadassah hospitals serve as a crucial bridge to peace, modeling a shared society through interfaith cooperation in daily clinical care and international medical collaboration. When terror, natural disasters or healthcare crises strike, Hadassah is on the frontlines. In the United States, Hadassah does more than support the compassionate care and research at its hospitals; it unites generations of women and families in purpose. Through dedicated support for Youth Aliyah Villages , Hadassah provides shelter, education, counseling, compassion and essential life skills to vulnerable teens and pre-teens in Israel, helping over 300,000 graduates build bright futures since 1934. At a time when the Jewish state and the global Jewish community face extraordinary challenges, Hadassah remains nonpartisan, advocating for women’s health equity; speaking out against hate and antisemitism; and championing a strong and secure Israel. Driven by a movement of women changemakers, the organization gives individuals the tools to lead, connect and create impact. At Hadassah, we believe that each of us has the potential to make a difference. How to get involved Healing the world takes action. There are ways to make an enduring impact: •       Become a member : Join a national network of nearly 300,000 women and advocates standing together for Israel and women's health. •       Support lifesaving research : Donate to fund pioneering medical research and state-of-the-art facilities and equipment at Hadassah hospitals. •       Advocate for change : Participate in national campaigns fighting antisemitism and anti-Zionism and advancing women’s health. Learn how you can be part of this legacy of hope and healing by exploring Our Impact . Visit: Hadassah.org .

title: Sotheby’s reaches deal with Jewish heirs over $180 million Van Gogh
description: Sotheby’s auction house announced on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement with the heirs of a German Jewish publisher over the contested sale of a Vincent van Gogh painting his family had sold in Amsterdam after the Nazis rose to power in Germany. “In recognition of the painting’s complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement,” Sotheby’s said in a statement , referring to the Fischer heirs and the painting's current owners. The agreement with the heirs of publisher Samuel Fischer concerned the “Châtaigniers en fleurs” (“Chestnut Trees in Blossom”), which is to be auctioned in New York on Wednesday and whose worth was estimated at $180 million. The terms of the agreement were not disclosed. The U.S.-based heirs, who had asked Sotheby’s to freeze the sale, said the 1890 work was sold in Amsterdam in 1936 because of financial losses their family’s publishing company suffered under Nazi rule. The Netherlands was not then under Nazi control, but the heirs argue that persecution in Germany forced the sale.

title: Jeffries wins House Democrats' speaker nomination despite progressive opposition
description: House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) for speaker on Wednesday, with only 11 members voting against him in a secret ballot. The nomination puts Jeffries on track to become speaker when the new Congress convenes in January. He must still win a vote of the full House. Seven newly elected progressive Democrats said in a statement that they voted against Jeffries because he had not committed to their priorities, including Medicare for All and ending the "genocide in Gaza." "There is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership," the statement said. It was signed by Reps.-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania.

description: Israel Police Commissioner Danny Levi reiterated on Wednesday that he had ordered the investigation into Haymanut Kasau's disappearance transferred to Lahav 433, the force's top crime and intelligence unit, as her family marked 1,000 days since she vanished from an immigrant absorption center in Safed. Levi said the move put the police's "leading and most professional" investigative unit on the case "in order to exhaust every line of inquiry and get to the truth." "We will not rest and we will not let up," he said, pledging to "turn over every stone" to locate the girl. He said he was personally following the probe and receiving ongoing updates. A "Justice for Haymanut" march was held in Tel Aviv on Wednesday evening, ending in a rally at Hostages Square with freed Hamas hostage Daniella Gilboa taking part, Kan News reported. Kasau was last seen on Feb. 25, 2024, outside the Jewish Agency absorption center where her family had been living since making aliyah from Ethiopia in 2021. A security camera captured her at the main entrance to the complex, where she had been distributing election pamphlets to residents.

title: Revolt-era hideouts and Byzantine church open to visitors in Judean Foothills
description: Tunnels where Jewish rebels sheltered some 2,000 years ago, alongside a Byzantine church paved with colorful mosaics, opened to the public this past weekend at Horvat Burgin in Adullam–France Park. The inauguration was a joint effort of KKL-JNF, the Israel Antiquities Authority and the Mateh Yehuda Regional Council, capping years of excavation, conservation and development. Digs led by Dr. Amir Ganor, Alon Klein and Dr. Peter Gendelman uncovered a settlement that endured from the Second Temple period through Ottoman times. Researchers suggest the large Second Temple village may be Caphar Bish, a place named by the historian Flavius Josephus. As tensions with Rome mounted in the Early Roman period, residents carved sprawling hiding networks into the bedrock. The settlement was destroyed during the Bar Kokhba Revolt of 132–136 CE. A pagan population later moved into the ruins, building anew above ground and cutting elaborate burial complexes beneath. In the Byzantine era, a church and monastery rose on the site. Dovecotes and winepresses found in the vicinity show that residents made their living from pigeon breeding, farming and winemaking. Ganor, who heads the Antiquities Authority’s Antiquities Theft Prevention Unit, described Horvat Burgin as the area’s largest ancient settlement. For years, he said, looters ravaged burial caves and tunnels and damaged standing structures. Enforcement operations, arrests of looting gangs, rescue excavations and the park’s opening finally stopped the destruction. “The site was saved,” Ganor said, “and now it can be enjoyed by the public.”

The Peruvian delegation included senior officers from national security agencies, counterterrorism experts and government representatives. Seventeen Israeli defense companies presented technologies tailored to the operational needs identified by Peru’s security agencies, including cybersecurity, drones and counter-drone systems, secure communications, VIP protection, intelligence gathering, big data and artificial intelligence. Participating companies included Robotican, Steadicopter, Roboteam, Rayzone Group, D-Fend Solutions and Netline Communications Technologies. According to the Defense Ministry, the initiative reflects Israel’s efforts to expand international security partnerships and open new markets for its defense industries.

"I am here on behalf of my comrades who saved the country: those who are still with us, those who were wounded and those who are no longer here." "Naturally, there is also a great deal of excitement and new experiences, but above all, there is a desire to shape the future for the younger generation in Israel," he said. "The issues I wish to advance concern those who serve, ensuring that those who sacrifice so much are placed at the very top of the state's list of priorities," Shalev said. title: Netanyahu's office slams Eisenkot letter as politicizing security
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office on Wednesday accused Yashar chief Gadi Eisenkot of politicizing national security, after the leader of the opposition bloc sent a letter urging him to avoid "dangerous moves" while a new government is being formed. The Prime Minister's Office called the missive "an irresponsible move to publicly discuss sensitive security issues." It said all decisions were made "solely out of security considerations" and "in full coordination with the security establishment." It added that Netanyahu "once again calls on Gadi Eisenkot to join the government that is fighting terrorism," rather than "trying to form a government with supporters of terrorism," in a reference to the opposition bloc's ongoing negotiations with Arab lawmakers. In his letter, Eisenkot had cited "very worrying reports" in recent weeks about "extraneous considerations" entering "the holy of holies: Israel's security." "I demand of you: In this sensitive period, you are required to show national responsibility," the missive said. Eisenkot urged "restraint and caution regarding dangerous moves that can wait for the swearing-in of a new government that wins the Knesset's confidence."

From Gaza ceasefire negotiations to U.S.-Israel relations and from Iran’s nuclear ambitions to the war on terror, Blum and Regev dissect the week’s headlines with authority, candor and a touch of humor. title: New analysis challenges Gaza famine, casualty claims using Hamas-run ministry data

The findings, published by the Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council (AIJAC) on Oct. 27, were highlighted by The Washington Free Beacon on Wednesday. The figures indicated natural population growth of approximately 1.2% in 2025, with 50,227 births and 24,650 registered deaths, including 5,780 classified as nonviolent. AIJAC argued that the mortality figures contradicted the United Nations-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification's August 2025 famine assessment, which also relied on malnutrition and food insecurity data. Of the 24,650 recorded deaths, 18,085, or 73.4%, were male, compared with 6,565 female deaths, or 26.6%. AIJAC said the figures challenged widely circulated claims that women and children accounted for 70% of casualties, although the breakdown did not establish how many of those killed were combatants. Israel's Foreign Ministry amplified the findings, saying that Hamas's figures were “not a reliable source.” Israeli Ambassador to the European Union Avi Nir-Feldklein also denounced accusations against Israel, writing, “The Genocide lie. The Apartheid lie.” He accused Israel's critics of seeking to demonize the Jewish state and obscure Hamas's crimes. The figures used by media to shape the global debate over Gaza have frequently come from Hamas’s own Ministry of Health. "The exception—if a letter is submitted bearing the signatures of a majority of MKs (at least 61 MKs) requesting to elect a speaker at an earlier date." "We will respect the Knesset members, and if a majority of them ask to hold such a debate, I will set it for an early date and no later than a week," he continued. "There will be no clinging to the horns of the altar," he wrote, using a Hebrew expression for refusing to give up power. "You can stop promoting conspiracy theories in the media." Yisrael Beytenu and The Democrats have sent Ohana letters asking him to put the election of a new speaker on the agenda of the 26th Knesset's first session on Tuesday, Hebrew media reported. The parties reportedly remain split over who should replace Ohana. Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad has proposed outgoing Opposition Leader Yair Lapid, the party's No. 2. Rabbi Menachem Margolin, chairman of the Brussels-based European Jewish Association, wrote on X: “We stand with the congregation and call on the authorities to establish what happened. Everyone should be able to enter a place of worship without fear.” Unia, Belgium’s equality body, received 192 reports of antisemitism in 2025. That was down from 277 in 2024 but up from 121 in 2023. Annual tallies in the two years before that were below 100. Belgium’s Jewish population fell from slightly more than 41,000 in 1980 to an estimated 28,900 in 2021, a drop of nearly 30%, according to a 2022 report by the Institute for Jewish Policy Research. The study found that Belgium had fewer Jews than it did in 1946, immediately after the Holocaust.

Last month, the Board of Deputies of British Jews labeled the Greens a “racist party” over a party resolution calling Zionism a form of racism. One user amplified by Polanski suggested that the March torching of ambulances belonging to a Jewish group in London was a “false flag.” The term is used to claim that Jews or Israel staged an attack to portray themselves as victims or to justify war. That user posts under the handle “Karl Marx.” Another account Polanski amplified, under the name “Jeremy David Parker,” falsely claimed that Hamas mostly targeted soldiers in its Oct. 7, 2023, massacre in Israel, the Daily Mail reported, citing the report. The Green Party did not respond to the Daily Mail ’s request for comment.

title: Hebrew University of Jerusalem presents honorary fellowship to philanthropist Dr. Wallace Weber
description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem presented an honorary fellowship to Dr. Wallace Weber during its 89th Board of Governors Meeting on Oct. 19 in Jerusalem. Weber is a retired dermatologist whose specialty practice expanded to include several offices throughout Kansas. He previously served in the Gulf War as a flight surgeon with the 82nd Airborne Division, later commanding the 410th U.S. Army Reserve Evacuation Hospital in Topeka. He retired from the U.S. Army after 31 years of service with awards including the Southwest Asia Service Medal and the Legion of Merit. Weber supports scholarships and regenerative agriculture at the Hebrew University's Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment, as well as other initiatives. He held a volunteer faculty appointment within the dermatology division at the University of Kansas School of Medicine, where he also created and endowed the university's annual lectureship, Military and Catastrophic Medicine. Weber was commissioned as a second lieutenant through the ROTC program at Colorado State University in 1965. He earned his medical degree from the University of Kansas School of Medicine in 1969. Professor Tamir Sheafer, president of the Hebrew University, bestowed the fellowship with the following citation: "in recognition of his long-standing support of Israel and the Hebrew University; in acknowledgement of his deep commitment to agricultural research and regenerative agriculture; in appreciation of his contribution to a safer world through many years of military service; in esteem for his remarkable career as a medical doctor and as an academic; in praise of his tireless efforts on behalf of the Hebrew University in the United States; and in deep gratitude for his generous donations to student scholarships and water research at the Hebrew University’s Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment." In accepting the honor, Weber stated, “It is an incredible and unexpected honor to be recognized by such a prestigious institution of higher learning as the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It is with much satisfaction and fondness for the accomplished members and staff of AFHU, as well as the staff, faculty and administration of the Jerusalem and Rehovot facilities, that I can reflect on my support journey over several decades.” Weber added, “It all started with a suggestion by one of the members of AFHU. The warmth and enthusiasm demonstrated in the initial contact with Beth McCoy [AFHU’s previous CEO] will ever be fond in my memory. Her staff’s ever-present willingness to help problem-solve and make me feel valued as a member of AFHU plays a major role in my support of this institution.”

title: Eisenkot vows to 'renew and deepen' US-Israel partnership
description: Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot addressed Israel’s friends in the United States and around the world in an X post on Wednesday, vowing to “renew and deepen” the partnership with Washington if he gets the mandate to form a government. “The Israeli people have voted for change and to replace the current government,” Eisenkot wrote in English. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc won 53 seats in the Oct. 27 Knesset election. The Zionist opposition parties—Yashar, B’Yachad (Together), The Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu—won 48. The Arab Joint List and Ra’am together secured 19 seats, leaving neither bloc with the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority. Eisenkot said he was working to form “a national emergency government” as soon as possible. He vowed to strengthen the “bipartisan foundations” of U.S.-Israel ties, adding that Jerusalem would remain “one of America’s most reliable and capable strategic partners in the Middle East.” Eisenkot said he looks forward to working “closely and constructively” with U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration. Trump endorsed Netanyahu on Oct. 18, nine days before the election, and again on Oct. 26, the eve of the vote. In his Oct. 18 endorsement , Trump explicitly linked further American action against Iran to Netanyahu’s re-election. “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” he wrote. To all our friends in the United States and around the world: The Israeli people have voted for change and to replace the current government. Our democracy remains strong and vibrant. We are working to fulfill the will of the Israeli people by forming a new government as soon… — Gadi Eisenkot - גדי איזנקוט (@gadi_eisenkot) November 4, 2026

title: Irish man gets suspended sentence for threatening Jews in France
description: An Irish man was handed a suspended sentence of six months in prison for threatening to kill a Jewish person near Marseille in August, French media reported on Tuesday. The man, identified in La Provence and other French media as Patrick O’Brien, 60, was filmed in Avignon in August telling an Australian Jewish couple that he regretted Adolf Hitler had not “finished the job,” expressing hope for Hitler's return and threatening to shoot the woman in the head. He admitted intending to hurt the couple verbally after realizing that the man was Jewish. In court, he described himself as a “great humanist,” La Provence said. The Avignon court convicted him of glorifying crimes against humanity and making death threats aggravated by antisemitic prejudice. He was ordered to pay €500 ($556) to each victim and €300 ($333) to several civil-party organizations. The court rejected prosecutors' request to ban him from French territory for three years. A lawyer representing the victims, Annie Cohen, said the sentence was excessively lenient, La Provence reported, noting that the woman's father was a Holocaust survivor. The incident had attracted widespread attention in France after a video of the confrontation went viral in August.

title: Australia weighs Iron Dome interceptors for air defense
description: Australia is considering buying interceptors developed for Israel’s Iron Dome as it seeks to field a ground-based missile defense system by the early 2030s, AFP reported on Thursday. Defense officials told a parliamentary committee that changes in warfare in Ukraine and the Middle East were driving the effort. Options include the U.S. Patriot system and interceptors developed by Israel’s Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and jointly manufactured with Raytheon. Air Marshal Robert Chipman said the Australian Defence Force would make recommendations to the government in 2027, following a competitive selection process linked to that year’s Talisman Sabre military exercise.

title: Japan, NCAG meet online to discuss Gaza reconstruction
description: Japan and the U.S.-backed National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) held their first formal working-group meeting on Wednesday to coordinate reconstruction efforts in the Gaza Strip, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry. The online meeting brought together Japanese Ambassador for Gaza Rebuilding Assistance Takeshi Okubo and NCAG Chief Commissioner Ali Shaath, it said. The NCAG welcomed Tokyo's commitment to “translating the Gaza Recovery Program into concrete action,” describing the meeting as “productive and encouraging.” Japanese officials reaffirmed their support for Gaza's recovery and discussed potential areas of cooperation, but no new funding or specific reconstruction projects were announced.
